title: Homogeneous quotient for a homomorphism with trivial scheme-theoretic kernel
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $H,G$ be separated finite-type $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $i:H\to G$ be a homomorphism whose scheme-theoretic kernel $H\times_{G,i,e_G}\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the trivial $k$-group scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. There exist a finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, a left $G$-action $\mu:G\times_k X\to X$, and a point $o:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$. Here a left action satisfies $\mu(e_G,x)=x$ and $\mu(g,\mu(g',x))=\mu(gg',x)$ on points over every $k$-scheme. Put $q(g)=\mu(g,o)$. For every $k$-scheme $T$ and every $a,b\in G(T)$ one has
$$q_T(a)=q_T(b)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a^{-1}b\in i_T(H(T)).$$
Here $Y(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_k(T,Y)$, and $o_T$ denotes the base change of $o$. No closed-immersion hypothesis is imposed on $i$.

source.place: Theorem 5.28, printed p.105, with Definition 5.20(a), printed p.104; Appendix B Theorem B.37, printed p.605 (the trivial-kernel, not closed-subgroup, version). The test-scheme coset equality is the affine-local form of Definition 5.20(a). Only the representability and coset-fibre conclusions are retained.

proof.text: The trivial scheme-theoretic kernel implies that $i_T:H(T)\to G(T)$ is injective for every $k$-scheme $T$: if $i_T(h)=i_T(h')$, then $h^{-1}h'$ factors through the kernel and is therefore the identity. Define a left $H$-action on $G$ by $h\cdot g=g\,i(h)^{-1}$. The equality $i(hh')^{-1}=i(h')^{-1}i(h)^{-1}$ proves the action law. If $h\cdot g=g$, cancellation and the established injectivity give $h=1$. Thus this action is free on all scheme tests, including nonreduced tests.

source.place: Proposition 5.31 and Appendix B, Example B.2; right-coset convention.

proof.text:
Regard $H,G$ as their representable algebraic spaces. The structure map of $H$ is flat by the field-flatness lemma; it is locally finitely presented by the locally-Noetherian lemma, since $k$ is a field and $H/k$ is finite type. Apply the free-flat-action quotient theorem to obtain the fppf sheaf $F=G/H$ and a surjective flat locally finitely presented map $q:G\to F$. Its kernel-pair isomorphism, after switching the two factors in the theorem's formula, is
$$G\times_kH\xrightarrow{\sim}G\times_FG,\qquad(g,h)\longmapsto(g,g\,i(h)).$$
Indeed the theorem's pair $(g i(h)^{-1},g)$ is of this form after replacing the first coordinate by $g i(h)^{-1}$. In particular $q_T(a)=q_T(b)$ if and only if $b=a i_T(h)$ for a unique $h\in H(T)$.

source.place: Tag 06PH, lemma-quotient-free-action; schemes are representable algebraic spaces.

proof.text: Left multiplication commutes with the right $H$-action and therefore defines a left $G$-action on $F$. Explicitly, for $g\in G(T)$ and $x\in F(T)$ choose the fppf local lifts $a_\alpha\in G(T_\alpha)$ of $x$ supplied by the quotient theorem and set $(g\cdot x)|_{T_\alpha}=q(g|_{T_\alpha}a_\alpha)$. On overlaps two lifts differ by right multiplication by $i(h)$, so their left translates have equal $q$-images by the kernel-pair formula. The sheaf property glues these sections uniquely; the same formula proves independence of lifts and naturality in $T$. On these covers the unit and associativity laws reduce to those of $G$, hence hold globally. Write $o_F=q(1)$; then $q(g)=g\cdot o_F$.

source.place: Theorem 5.28 and Appendix B Theorem B.37: the action on the quotient; explicit local-section construction.

proof.text: The diagonal of $F/k$ is quasi-compact, without first asserting separatedness. Its pullback by the fppf covering $q\times q:G\times_kG\to F\times_kF$ is the morphism $G\times_kH\to G\times_kG$ of Step 2. The source is quasi-compact: finite affine covers of $G$ and $H$ give a finite cover by affine products. The target is quasi-separated: it is separated over the affine field spectrum, so its relative diagonal is closed and its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. The qcqs permanence lemma therefore makes this morphism quasi-compact. The covering calculus gives that $q\times q$ is fppf (base change and composition of $q$), and quasi-compactness descends along this covering by the quasi-compactness descent lemma. This verifies exactly the diagonal hypothesis of the dense-scheme-open theorem.

source.place: Tag 041L, lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 073B; spaces-topologies.tex Tag 03Y9.

proof.text: The quotient $F$ is finite type over $k$. The source-descent lemma applies to $G\xrightarrow qF\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: these are algebraic-space morphisms, $q$ is surjective flat lfp, and their composite is locally finite type. Thus $F/k$ is locally finite type. The continuous surjection $|G|\to|F|$ makes $|F|$ quasi-compact. By the qcqs permanence lemma (whose quasi-compact-space convention is the point-topological one), $F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact because the target is affine and quasi-separated. Combining the two properties gives finite type. Notice that this argument needs no separatedness of $F$.

By the dense-scheme-open theorem and Step 4, $F$ contains a dense scheme open $V$. It is nonempty since $q(1)$ is a point of $F$. For each finite intermediate extension $K$ in a fixed algebraic closure of $k$, let $V[K]=(F_K)_{\mathrm{sch}}$ be the largest scheme open supplied by the schematic-open lemma. It contains $V_K$. Translation by an element of $G(K)$ is an automorphism of $F_K$ and carries a scheme open to a scheme open; applying the same observation to its inverse proves that it preserves $V[K]$. For $K\subseteq K'$, the base change $(V[K])_{K'}$ is a scheme open of $F_{K'}$, hence is contained in $V[K']$. These assertions concern open subspaces and therefore also their inverse images in $G_K$.

source.place: Appendix B Theorem B.37, Step 1; dense generic quotient implemented by Stacks Tags 086U and 03JH.

proof.text: The inverse image $q^{-1}(V)$ is a nonempty open of the finite-type scheme $G$. Take a nonempty principal affine open inside it and a maximal ideal of its nonzero finite-type $k$-algebra. Zariski's lemma makes the residue field finite over $k$. Embed it in the fixed algebraic closure; thus for some finite $k_1/k$ there is $g_0\in G(k_1)$ whose image lies in $V[k_1]$. For every finite $K/k_1$ and $g\in G(K)$, translation by $g g_0^{-1}$ sends $q(g_0)$ to $q(g)$; invariance of $V[K]$ gives $q(G(K))\subseteq V[K]$. Apply the existing finite-extension exhaustion lemma to $Z=G_{k_1}$ and the compatible opens $U[K]=q_K^{-1}(V[K])$, which contain all $K$-rational points. It gives $U[K]=G_K$ for some finite $K/k_1$. Base-change surjectivity of $q$ then gives $V[K]=F_K$. Consequently $F_K$ is a scheme $Y$, finite type over $K$ by base-change stability of finite type.

source.place: Appendix B Lemma B.36 and Theorem B.37, Step 1, printed pp.604-605.

proof.text: We can now prove that $i$ is closed using only the scheme quotient over $K$. The rational point $o_K=q_K(1):\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ has residue field $K$, so its image is closed by the closed-point field criterion for finite-type schemes. The residue-point immersion lemma makes $o_K$ a closed immersion. Base changing the kernel-pair formula of Step 2 along $1:\operatorname{Spec}K\to G_K$ identifies $H_K$ with $G_K\times_{Y,o_K}\operatorname{Spec}K$, compatibly with $i_K$. Hence $i_K$ is a closed immersion, as the base change of the closed immersion $o_K$ along $q_K$ by the closed-immersion base-change lemma. A finite basis of $K/k$ makes $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ finite flat, surjective and locally finitely presented; the same is true after base change to $G$. Closed-immersion fppf descent applied to $i$ and the cover $G_K\to G$ proves that $i$ is a closed immersion. No monomorphism-to-closed-immersion theorem has been used.

source.place: Theorem 5.34, first proof, applied after the finite extension of Appendix B Theorem B.37 Step 1; descent: Stacks Tag 0420.

proof.text: Apply the existing closed-subgroup homogeneous quotient theorem to the now-established closed subgroup $i:H\hookrightarrow G$. It supplies a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ and a flat surjective finitely presented $p:G\to X$ with the same right-coset fibre relation as $q$. Its hypotheses on $H,G$ and on closedness have all been verified. The scheme and quotient map are obtained at this point over the original field $k$.

source.place: Theorem 5.28, closed-subgroup case, as independently split in lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient.

proof.text: Identify $X$ with $F$ as fppf sheaves. For $x\in F(T)$, take fppf local lifts $a_\alpha:T_\alpha\to G$ and assign $p(a_\alpha)$. Their equality on overlaps follows from the common coset relation; the fppf-sheaf property of the representable algebraic space $X$ glues them to a unique section of $X(T)$. Conversely the flat surjective finitely presented morphism $p$ gives fppf local lifts of every $X(T)$-section: its scheme pullback along $T\to X$ is itself an fppf covering by the definition of the big fppf site. Apply the same construction with $q$ and the fppf-sheaf property of $F$. The two transformations are natural and inverse, since on local lifts their composites send $a$ back to its original image. Thus the identification carries $p$ to $q$. It transports the natural action from Step 3 to a morphism $\mu:G\times_kX\to X$: a natural transformation between representable functors is the morphism obtained by evaluating it on the identity of its source. Put $o=p(1)$. The already verified action laws give $p(g)=\mu(g,o)$.

source.place: Theorem 5.28 and Definition 5.20; explicit comparison of the quotient fppf sheaves.

proof.text:
For any $k$-scheme $T$, Step 10 identifies the required orbit map with $p_T$. The coset-fibre equality in the closed-subgroup quotient theorem therefore reads
$$q_T(a)=q_T(b)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a^{-1}b\in i_T(H(T)).$$
The quotient theorem quantifies over every scheme $T$, so this includes non-affine and nonreduced schemes. The finite-type property of $X$, its action and its $k$-point have all been obtained without an initial closed-immersion assumption on $i$.

source.place: Definition 5.20(a) and Theorem 5.28, the claimed clauses.

lean.statement: theorem exists_homogeneousQuotient_of_trivialKernel (k : Type u) [Field k] (H G : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj H] [GrpObj G] [IsSeparated H.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType H.hom] [QuasiCompact H.hom] [IsSeparated G.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] (i : H ⟶ G) [IsMonHom i] (hker : IsIso (toUnit (GrpObj.ker i))) : ∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) (act : ModObj G X) (o : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ X), LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ QuasiCompact X.hom ∧ ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (a b : T ⟶ G), lift a (toUnit T ≫ o) ≫ act.smul = lift b (toUnit T ≫ o) ≫ act.smul ↔ a⁻¹ * b ∈ Set.range (fun h : T ⟶ H ↦ h ≫ i)
lean.note: Mathlib's ModObj G X is the left action morphism with unit and associativity laws.
